findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards recorded logs
findings.body: pkg/plugins/log/fake.go FromContext returns NewTestLogger() instead of the receiver. pkg/services/pluginsintegration/clientmiddleware/logger_middleware.go now logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...). When the injected logger is a TestLogger, the Info call goes to a fresh instance, so callers asserting on the original TestLogger see 0 calls and lose message/ctx. The fake diverges from the real wrapper which derives from the base logger, breaking test observability.

findings.title: New ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics on nil request
findings.body: ContextualLoggerMiddleware QueryData, CallResource, CheckHealth and CollectMetrics dereference req (e.g. req.PluginContext) without a nil check. LoggerMiddleware in the same package explicitly guards req==nil and passes through. Because CreateMiddlewares places ContextualLoggerMiddleware outside LoggerMiddleware, a nil request panics in the new middleware before the existing guard is reached, turning a pass-through case into a crash.

findings.title: LoggerMiddleware loses explicit fields and depends on outer middleware
findings.body: logger_middleware.go removed explicit pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName, dsUID and traceID from logParams and now relies on m.logger.FromContext(ctx) populated by ContextualLoggerMiddleware. The new contextual_logger_middleware.go instrumentContext only adds endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname and does not add traceID that the old logRequest added via tracing.TraceIDFromContext. Result: Plugin Request Completed logs lose trace correlation, and any use of LoggerMiddleware without the new middleware in front of it or in a different order silently loses plugin context that was previously self-contained.
